recentItems.title: Why your inner dialogue shapes how the world hears you | Kunal Buch | TEDxMITWPU
recentItems.description:
You can't fix the output without changing the input. Dr. Kunal Buch, voice, power and personality coach, shares why true vocal authority begins in the voice within, and gives you a simple 21-day practice to start changing it today.


What are you really checking when you look in the mirror each morning? Dr. Kunal Buch argues it's not your face or your clothes, but your inner voice.

This talk explores how our internal dialogue shapes confidence, presence and communication, drawing on research by Ethan Kross, Ozlem Ayduk, and Killingsworth and Gilbert. You'll learn why communication is what we think + what we feel + how we sound + how we express it, and take away a three-part practice to try for 21 days: a morning voice check, a midday energy check, and three nightly wins. Kunal Buch is a renowned Anchor, Author, Life Coach and Entertainer, known for his energetic stage presence and exceptional ability to connect with audiences. With over two decades of experience, he has hosted and entertained at numerous prestigious events. A trained performer and versatile personality, Kunal combines communication, storytelling and life experiences to inspire and engage people. His work as an author and life coach further reflects his passion for personal growth and meaningful connections. This talk was given at a TEDx event using the TED conference format but independently organized by a local community. Learn more at https://www.ted.com/tedx

recentItems.title: Build Your Second Lane Before You Need It | Ian Issa | TEDxSukhna Lake
recentItems.description:
What happens when the one thing you have built your life around suddenly disappears?

In this thought-provoking talk, Ian Issa shares how a career-ending athletic injury forced him to rebuild his identity and discover a new path. Years later, he recognised the same vulnerability in the cryptocurrency mining industry, where businesses were investing heavily in a single outcome without preparing for what might come next.

Drawing parallels between his personal journey and business strategy, Ian introduces the idea of a “second lane” — an alternative skill, capability or pursuit developed before it becomes necessary.

He challenges us to step outside our comfort zones, learn things we are not yet good at, build relationships beyond our immediate circles and prepare for change while things are still going well.

His message is simple: resilience isn't just about recovering when something goes wrong. It's about creating options before you need them.

 Ian Issa is the Founder & CEO of HashNet Infrastructure LLC, a Dubai-based cryptocurrency mining company built on the belief that resilient systems are designed, not left to chance. Since entering the digital assets space in 2017, he has founded three companies, with two successful exits, spanning machine learning, decentralized finance, and blockchain infrastructure. Before entrepreneurship, Ian was a national-level athlete, competing while studying in the US until a career-ending injury reshaped his path.

Today, he speaks to institutional investors, entrepreneurs, and business leaders on identifying hidden vulnerabilities, building resilient systems, and distinguishing design failures from market failures. His ideas challenge conventional thinking on risk, resilience, and the decisions that shape lasting success. This talk was given at a TEDx event using the TED conference format but independently organized by a local community. Learn more at https://www.ted.com/tedx

recentItems.title: Fofoca: a ferramenta que construiu a humanidade | Laura Marise | TEDxUNISO
recentItems.description:
E se a fofoca, tão frequentemente associada a algo fútil ou maldoso, fosse uma das ferramentas mais importantes para a construção da humanidade?

Nesta palestra, Laura Marise propõe uma nova perspectiva sobre um comportamento universal: a troca de informações sobre outras pessoas e acontecimentos. Mais do que falar da vida alheia, a fofoca pode ajudar a construir redes de confiança, fortalecer vínculos sociais e favorecer a cooperação entre indivíduos.

Com humor e exemplos do cotidiano, Laura explora como a circulação de informações influencia nossas relações e nos convida a olhar para a própria ciência sob uma perspectiva inusitada: afinal, o que são artigos científicos, congressos e revisões por pares senão diferentes formas de compartilhar, discutir e avaliar descobertas?

Uma reflexão sobre conexões, conhecimento e comportamento humano que desafia nossas percepções e deixa uma provocação: será que a ciência é a forma mais sofisticada de fofoca que já inventamos?

Sobre a palestrante

Laura Marise é farmacêutica-bioquímica formada pela UNESP, mestre e doutora em Biociências e Biotecnologia pela mesma instituição, com pós-doutorado em Bioquímica pela USP. Há oito anos atua como comunicadora e divulgadora científica. É cofundadora, ao lado de Ana Bonassa, do projeto Nunca Vi 1 Cientista, dedicado a desmistificar conceitos científicos e aproximar a ciência do público por meio de conteúdos informativos e educativos. Ela é farmacêutica-bioquímica formada pela UNESP, mestra e doutora em biociências e biotecnologia pela mesma instituição, com pós-doutorado em bioquímica pela USP. Atua há 8 anos como comunicadora e divulgadora científica. É cofundadora do perfil Nunca Vi 1 Cientista, ao lado de Ana Bonassa, onde juntas desmistificam conceitos científicos e tornam a ciência mais acessível ao público por meio de conteúdos informativos e educativos. recentItems.title: Who Is the African Woman Really - Na Who She Be? | Dr. Zina Arinze | TEDxKubwa
recentItems.description:
In this compelling TEDx talk, Dr. Zina Arinze, widely known as The Reinvention Queen, challenges conventional perceptions of African womanhood, exploring the intersection of identity, culture, resilience and self-definition. Drawing from over 25 years of experience in law, technology, leadership and personal reinvention, alongside her journey across different countries and cultures, she invites audiences to look beyond stereotypes and recognise the complexity, strength and individuality of African women. Through her experiences of career transformation, divorce and rediscovering herself, Dr. Arinze examines how societal expectations can shape women's identities and why reclaiming the power to define oneself is essential to personal freedom and fulfilment. Her message is both a celebration and a challenge: the African woman is not a single story, a fixed identity or a reflection of society's expectations. She is a person with the power to define, reinvent and own her narrative. Dr. Zina Arinze, known as The Reinvention Queen, is a multi-award-winning Leadership Reinvention Coach, international speaker, lawyer, best-selling author and global Technology Transformation Leader with over 25 years’ experience. After practising corporate law, she reinvented into technology, leading major transformation initiatives across international teams.

As Founder of The Reinvent YOU Experience, she helps high-achieving women reinvent their influence, impact and income, while helping organisations strengthen leadership and create cultures where women can progress and lead.

A Fellow of the Institute of Enterprise and Entrepreneurs, her work advances women’s participation and leadership. Her lived experience across countries, careers and cultures, including divorce and a later-life ADHD diagnosis, informs her work on identity and reinvention. She is the author of Reinvent YOU! How to Move from We to Me after Divorce, now being reimagined for its 10th Anniversary Edition. This talk was given at a TEDx event using the TED conference format but independently organized by a local community. Learn more at https://www.ted.com/tedx
